lock_reason: Not locked, and the recorded selection is RETIRED rather than reversed. The muon_polar_adamw / normuon_adamw ordering CROSSES OVER in learning rate. muon_polar_adamw leads at the low end, normuon_adamw at the high end, each sign-consistent across all seeds tested. There is no recipe-independent answer to which optimizer is better at this scale. exact_128m_1000 compared muon_polar_adamw at lr 0.05 against normuon_adamw at lr 0.1 -- both far up the high-LR wall, on one side of a crossing it had no way to see -- and recorded a 0.031226 BPB margin. That margin measures the learning rates, not the optimizers. Inherited-LR penalties: muon_polar_adamw 0.046020 +/- 0.003175 = 1.474x the 0.031226 selection margin; normuon_adamw 0.080400 (n=2, sign test only) = 2.575x the 0.031226 selection margin. Do not lock on muon_polar_adamw, and do not lock on normuon_adamw either: at each candidate's own best tested cell the paired gap is +0.004097 +/- 0.005085, which spans zero. A lock needs a bracketed optimum for both candidates at a shared protocol; bracketed is muon_polar_adamw=False, normuon_adamw=False. Derived by scripts/d7_analyze.py from research/d7-lr-retune.json; do not edit by hand.

limits: Sign tests are the primary evidence. Only 3 of 8 matched cells have an interval excluding zero; the effects are at or below the per-cell seed sd of ~0.006.
Neither candidate's optimum is a POINT: both have flat basins whose interior minimum is not resolvable at n=3.
One protocol only: arch02-128m, 1000 steps, Metal/M5. Nothing here transfers to other scales, horizons or hardware.
Wall-clock and step timings from these runs are contended and must not be quoted as throughput.
